title: Performance corridor SLA and degradation allowance — contract-ready language and measurement plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: produce a contract-ready SLA model for Dedicated Capacity that avoids brittle per-minute credits and instead defines a performance corridor and a degradation allowance. The proposal covers SLO definitions, the error-budget-like 'degradation allowance', measurement windows, escalation triggers, credit calculation examples, and legal wording for enterprise contracts.

Key concepts: 
- Performance corridor: a range of expected throughput and 95th/99th token-latency boundaries per entitlement tier rather than single-point guarantees. This allows predictable application behavior while limiting noise from rare spikes.
- Degradation allowance: a bounded amount of short-term deviation from the corridor (measured in throughput-seconds) that acts like an error budget but is expressed in capacity-time; customers consume allowance when observed throughput falls below entitlement or latency exceeds thresholds.
- Rolling windows and smoothing: measure over 24h and 30-day windows with exponential smoothing for bursty tenants; short windows drive immediate remediation/autoscale, long windows drive credits.
- Autoscale interplay: defined stabilization windows and minimum ramp guarantees so autoscaling does not create oscillation that would itself trigger credit events.
- Credit mechanics: credits are computed from the integral of under-served throughput over the billing period, subject to per-incident caps and a maximum monthly credit percentage. Example formulas and worked scenarios included.
- Exceptions: planned maintenance, force majeure, and customer misconfiguration are explicitly excluded. A transparent incident-dispute process is defined with evidence artifacts (per-tenant metrics, request traces, sample logs).

Measurement / Instrumentation notes: metrics required from serving runtime and console: per-tenant allocated capacity, observed served TPS, queue length distributions, token-latency P95/P99, autoscale events and reasons, pre- and post-fallback model variants served. We propose adding a per-tenant "capacity-entitlement" telemetry stream to the observability pipeline to avoid reconciliation gaps.

Contract language highlights (summary):
- Definition sections for "Performance Corridor", "Degradation Allowance", "Measurement Window", "Remediation Credits" and "Excluded Events".
- Escalation: automated remediation (autoscale to burst), followed by human review within 4 hours, and formal credit determination within 14 calendar days.
- Cap on credits: monthly max of 20% of the Dedicated invoice for that subscription, with per-incident cap equal to 10% of monthly invoice.

Trade-offs considered:
- Conservative corridors reduce customer surprise but increase Redwood's operational headroom.
- Degradation allowance provides predictable legal boundaries at the cost of more complex measurement and customer education.
- Tighter SLAs with smaller credits require higher reserved overhead and will be priced accordingly.

Deliverables: contract-ready clause set, measurement spec for ENG, console dashboard mockups for customer-facing SLA state, billing engine hook for crediting, and legal sign-off checklist.

2026-02-26 — Eng feedback: runtime can emit per-tenant entitlement and served-throughput streams with low overhead. Concern: P99 collection granularity for high-throughput tenants needs sampling. Action: adjust measurement to sample P99 with deterministic reservoir and include sample-rate metadata.
2026-03-01 — Design (Hannah Liu) produced SLA visualization mockups showing corridor bands and depletion of degradation allowance; uploaded: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/perf-corridor-v1

2026-03-04 — Legal (Noah Reynolds) requested explicit wording for 'Excluded Events' and clearer dispute timelines; suggested limiting per-incident evidence window to 90 days. Updated draft clause accordingly.

2026-03-07 — Product review: agreed on rolling 24h short-window for autoscale trigger and 30-day long-window for credit calculation. Decided on monthly maximum credit 20% and per-incident cap 10%. Action: route to billing infra and invoices team (ENG-10145) for implementation feasibility.

2026-03-10 — Internal review meeting notes: follow-ups assigned — Miguel to produce contract redline, ENG to provide sample metric export (due 2026-03-18), Legal to prepare final clause language (due 2026-03-20).
Next steps — finalize contract redline, implement per-tenant entitlement telemetry spike-proofing, add SLA state to Console beta, and schedule legal sign-off meeting week of 2026-03-22.
